es.B: El Cantar de los Cantares, el más grande de los cantos, que es de Salomón.

fr.R: Le plus beau des chants. Il est de Salomon.

sw.B: Wimbo wa Nyimbo, wimbo bora kuliko nyimbo zote, ulio wa Sulemani.
sw.R: Wimbo mzuri kuliko nyimbo zote. Ni wa Sulemani.

vi.L: Bài ca của các bài ca, [là bài ca] của Sa-lô-môn.
vi.B: Bài ca của các bài ca, bài ca tuyệt vời nhất, là của Sa-lô-môn.

ko.B: 노래 중의 노래, 가장 빼어난 노래, 솔로몬의 노래이다.

decisions.choice: the song of songs: the finest song of all
alternatives: the song made of songs (a collection)
decisions.reason: Hebrew makes a superlative by joining a word to its own plural: "the holy of holies" is the most holy place (Exodus 26:33), "king of kings" the greatest king (Ezra 7:12). So the title calls this the best of all songs. "Song of Songs" stays the name of the book.

decisions.choice: which is Solomon's: by, for, or about Solomon
decisions.reason: The small word in front of Solomon's name (le-) can mean "by", "for", "about" or "belonging to", as in the psalm titles "of David" (Psalm 3:1). The title may name Solomon as the author, dedicate the song to him, or say it is about him; he appears in the poem as a figure (3:7, 9, 11; 8:11-12). Solomon was king of Israel in the tenth century BC and was remembered for his many songs (1 Kings 5:12, which is 4:32 in many Bibles). The words keep this open.

decisions.choice: how the Song has been read: the translation follows the plain sense of a poem about the love of a woman and a man
alternatives: an allegory of God and Israel
an allegory of Christ and the Church
decisions.reason: The Song never mentions God by name (but see 8:6) and speaks of the love, desire and union of two lovers. Jewish tradition has long read it as a picture of God's love for Israel, and it is read at Passover. Christian tradition has read it as Christ's love for the Church or for the soul. Many modern readers read it as a poem, or a collection of poems, about human love, which the Bible elsewhere also celebrates (Genesis 2:23-25; Proverbs 5:18-19). The translation renders what the words say about the lovers; it leaves the larger readings to the reader and adds no wording that belongs to any one of them.

decisions.choice: the Song has no named speakers; the speaker is noted where each speech begins
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no names or stage directions, but its verbs and pronouns show whether a man or a woman speaks or is spoken to, and whether one person or a group. A decision at the first verse of each speech says who speaks, and marks it uncertain where the forms do not settle it. The title itself is spoken by no one in the poem.

decisions.choice: the greatest of songs; The most beautiful of songs
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the title "The Song of Songs" and adds what the superlative means; Readable says only what it means. The book is still called the Song of Songs.

decisions.choice: Solomon's
decisions.reason: The possessive keeps the Hebrew open: it can mean written by, given to, or about Solomon (m2).

decisions.choice: "El Cantar de los Cantares"
decisions.reason: "El Cantar de los Cantares" is the name of the book in Spanish and keeps the Hebrew way of making a superlative (a word joined to its own plural); Balanced then adds what it means, "el más grande de los cantos", and Readable says only that.

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: no speaker labels and no quotation marks; Spanish agreement shows who speaks ("morena soy", "hermoso eres"); no divine_name span except 8:6 at Literal and no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: labels such as "Ella" / "Él" before each speech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names no speakers; its verb and pronoun forms show them, and Spanish adjectives and participles agree in the same way. The voices take no quotation marks, as in the Psalms; only words quoted inside a speech do (2:10; 5:2). The Song does not name God, except possibly in 8:6.

decisions.choice: "Le Cantique des cantiques"
decisions.reason: "Le Cantique des cantiques" is the name of the book in French and keeps the Hebrew superlative; Balanced adds "le plus grand des chants" and Readable gives only the sense, "le plus beau des chants".

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: the voices are speech, so present, future and passé composé at every level, never the passé simple; "tu" between the lovers, "vous" to the women of Jerusalem; no speaker labels, no quotation marks
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The Song has no narrator: every line is someone speaking, so it uses the tenses of speech. French agreement ("je suis noire", "tu es beau") shows who speaks, as the Hebrew forms do, and no labels are added. There is no divine_name span except 8:6 at Literal, and no deity_pronoun spans.

decisions.choice: "Wimbo wa Nyimbo"
decisions.reason: "Wimbo wa Nyimbo" keeps the Hebrew way of making a superlative, which Balanced explains ("wimbo bora kuliko nyimbo zote"); "Wimbo Ulio Bora" (the song that is best) is the name many Swahili readers know for the book, and says the sense rather than the words.

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: no speaker labels and no quotation marks; the words of address ("mpendwa wangu", "mpenzi wangu", "bibi arusi") show who speaks
decisions.reason: Swahili verbs and adjectives do not show whether a man or a woman speaks, as the Hebrew forms do; the meaning decisions name the speaker, and the drafts keep the words of address that make it clear. No divine_name span except 8:6 at Literal.

decisions.choice: "Bài ca của các bài ca"
decisions.reason: "Nhã Ca" is the name of the book in Vietnamese Bibles, but it does not say what the title says; "Bài ca của các bài ca" keeps the Hebrew superlative, and Balanced adds "bài ca tuyệt vời nhất".

decisions.choice: "노래 중의 노래"
decisions.reason: "아가" is the book's name in Korean Bibles but does not show the title's wording; "노래 중의 노래" keeps the Hebrew superlative in natural Korean, and Balanced adds "가장 빼어난 노래".

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: no speaker labels, no quotation marks, no deity_pronoun spans, and a divine_name span only at 8:6 Literal
decisions.reason: Korean pronouns do not show whether a man or a woman speaks; the words of address (내 사랑하는 이 for him, 나의 연인 for her, 신부) and the meaning decisions carry it, so no labels are added to the poem.

source.text: יִשָּׁקֵ֨נִי֙ מִנְּשִׁיק֣וֹת פִּ֔יהוּ כִּֽי־טוֹבִ֥ים דֹּדֶ֖יךָ מִיָּֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: Let him kiss me with [the] kisses of his mouth, for better [is] your lovemaking than wine.

en.L: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, \q for better [is] your lovemaking than wine.
en.B: May he kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! \q Your love is better than wine.
en.R: Oh, how I want him to kiss me! \q Your love is more delightful than wine.

es.L: Que me bese con los besos de su boca, \q porque mejores [son] tus caricias que el vino.
es.B: ¡Que me bese con los besos de su boca! \q Tu amor es mejor que el vino.
es.R: ¡Cuánto deseo que me bese! \q Tu amor es más delicioso que el vino.

fr.L: Qu’il m’embrasse des baisers de sa bouche, \q car meilleures [sont] tes caresses que le vin.
fr.B: Qu’il me donne les baisers de sa bouche ! \q Ton amour est meilleur que le vin.
fr.R: Oh, comme je voudrais qu’il m’embrasse ! \q Ton amour est plus délicieux que le vin.

sw.L: Anibusu kwa mabusu ya kinywa chake, \q kwa maana mahaba yako [ni] bora kuliko divai.
sw.B: Laiti angenibusu kwa mabusu ya kinywa chake! \q Mapenzi yako ni bora kuliko divai.
sw.R: Natamani sana anibusu! \q Mapenzi yako yanapendeza kuliko divai.

vi.L: Ước gì chàng hôn em bằng những nụ hôn của miệng chàng, \q vì ân ái của anh [thì] tốt hơn rượu.
vi.B: Ước gì chàng hôn em bằng những nụ hôn của môi chàng! \q Tình yêu của anh tuyệt hơn rượu.
vi.R: Ôi, em mong chàng hôn em biết bao! \q Tình yêu của anh còn ngọt ngào hơn rượu.

ko.L: 그가 자기 입의 입맞춤으로 내게 입 맞추었으면, \q 그대의 사랑이 포도주보다 좋기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그가 그 입술로 내게 입 맞추어 주었으면! \q 그대의 사랑은 포도주보다 좋다.
ko.R: 아, 그가 내게 입 맞춰 주면 좋겠어요! \q 당신의 사랑은 포도주보다 달콤해요.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks (1:2-7)
decisions.reason: The one who speaks longs for "him"; in 1:5-6 she describes herself with feminine forms ("black", "lovely", "darkened"), so the Song opens with the woman's voice.

decisions.choice: from "him" to "you": she speaks of him and then to him
decisions.reason: The verse moves from "his mouth" to "your lovemaking" without warning. Such shifts of person are common in Hebrew poetry (Psalm 23:1-4) and are kept as they are.

decisions.choice: lovemaking: the acts and caresses of love
decisions.reason: The plural word (dodim) is not the general word for love ('ahavah) but its physical expression: kisses, caresses, making love (Proverbs 7:18; Ezekiel 16:8; 23:17). It returns in 1:4; 4:10; 5:1; 7:13.

decisions.choice: love
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "love", which in a love song carries the physical sense; Literal says "lovemaking" to show that the word is about touch, not only feeling (m3).

decisions.choice: Oh, how I want him to kiss me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the wish of the verb form ("let him kiss me") as a longing and leaves "the kisses of his mouth", a doubled phrase, as plain kissing.

decisions.choice: "caricias" for dodim at Literal; "amor" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Dodim is love shown in touch (meaning decision m3); "caricias" says so at Literal, as Proverbs 7:18 does, and "amor" carries it in a love song at the other levels. This holds for the whole Song (1:4; 4:10; 5:1; 7:13).

decisions.choice: "embrasser" for the verb "kiss"
decisions.reason: The verb "baiser" is now a vulgar word for sex in everyday French; "embrasser" is the ordinary verb for kissing. The noun "les baisers" keeps its plain sense and stays.

decisions.choice: "tes caresses" for dodim at Literal; "ton amour" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Dodim is love shown in touch (m3); "caresses" says so at Literal, as Proverbs 7:18 does. This holds for the whole Song.

decisions.choice: "mahaba" for dodim at Literal; "mapenzi" at Balanced and Readable; "upendo" for 'ahavah
decisions.reason: "Mahaba" is the love of lovers, shown in touch (m3), as Proverbs 7:18; "mapenzi" is the everyday word for romantic love; "upendo" is kept for the general word 'ahavah (2:4, 7; 8:6-7). This holds for the whole Song.

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: she says "anh" to him and "em" for herself, he says "em" to her and "anh" for himself; speaking of each other, "chàng" and "nàng"; to the women of Jerusalem she says "các chị" and "tôi"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese pronouns name the relation between speaker and hearer: "anh" and "em" are what lovers call each other, and "chàng" and "nàng" are the poetic words for a lover spoken of. Here the verse moves from "him" (chàng) to "you" (anh), as the Hebrew does (m2).

decisions.choice: "ân ái" for dodim at Literal; "tình yêu" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Dodim is love shown in touch (m3); "ân ái" says so, as Proverbs 7:18 does. This holds for the whole Song.

decisions.choice: For the whole Song: the lovers call each other "그대" in the plain poetic style at Literal and Balanced, and "당신" in 해요체 at Readable; speaking of him she says "그" or "그이"
decisions.reason: "그대" is the warm, poetic "you" of Korean love poetry and suits the plain style of the Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the spoken 해요체 with "당신", as between a couple today. 그녀 is not used.

decisions.choice: "입 맞추었으면" for the wish "let him kiss me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew form is a wish, not a command to anyone; Korean says a wish with -었으면, which keeps it as longing.

source.text: לְרֵ֨יחַ֙ שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִ֔ים שֶׁ֖מֶן תּוּרַ֣ק שְׁמֶ֑ךָ עַל־כֵּ֖ן עֲלָמ֥וֹת אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For fragrance your oils [are] good; oil poured out [is] your name; therefore young women love you.

en.L: For fragrance your oils [are] pleasing; \q your name [is] oil poured out; \q therefore the young women love you.
en.B: The scent of your perfumes is lovely; \q your name is perfume poured out; \q that is why the young women love you.
en.R: Your perfume smells wonderful. \q Your name is like sweet perfume poured out. \q That is why the young women love you.

es.L: Por su fragancia tus aceites [son] agradables; \q tu nombre [es] aceite derramado; \q por eso las jóvenes te aman.
es.B: El aroma de tus perfumes es delicioso; \q tu nombre es perfume que se derrama; \q por eso te aman las jóvenes.
es.R: Tu perfume huele de maravilla. \q Tu nombre es como un perfume dulce que se derrama. \q Por eso las jóvenes te aman.

fr.L: Pour le parfum, tes huiles [sont] agréables ; \q ton nom [est] une huile répandue ; \q c’est pourquoi les jeunes femmes t’aiment.
fr.B: Tes parfums ont une odeur délicieuse ; \q ton nom est un parfum qu’on verse ; \q voilà pourquoi les jeunes femmes t’aiment.
fr.R: Ton parfum sent si bon. \q Ton nom est comme un doux parfum qu’on répand. \q Voilà pourquoi les jeunes femmes t’aiment.

sw.L: Kwa harufu mafuta yako [ni] mazuri; \q jina lako [ni] mafuta yaliyomiminwa; \q kwa hiyo wanawali wanakupenda.
sw.B: Harufu ya manukato yako inapendeza; \q jina lako ni manukato yanayomiminwa; \q ndiyo maana wasichana wanakupenda.
sw.R: Manukato yako yananukia vizuri sana. \q Jina lako ni kama manukato matamu yaliyomiminwa. \q Ndiyo sababu wasichana wanakupenda.

vi.L: Về hương thơm, dầu của anh [thật] dễ chịu; \q danh anh [là] dầu được đổ ra; \q vì thế các thiếu nữ yêu anh.
vi.B: Hương dầu thơm của anh thật ngào ngạt; \q danh anh là dầu thơm tuôn đổ; \q vì vậy các thiếu nữ đều yêu anh.
vi.R: Dầu thơm của anh tỏa hương thật tuyệt. \q Tên anh như dầu thơm ngọt ngào được đổ ra. \q Vì thế các cô gái trẻ yêu anh.

ko.L: 향기로 말하면 그대의 기름들이 좋고, \q 그대의 이름은 쏟아 부은 기름이다. \q 그러므로 젊은 여자들이 그대를 사랑한다.
ko.B: 그대의 향유는 향기가 좋고, \q 그대의 이름은 쏟아 부은 향유이니, \q 그래서 젊은 여자들이 그대를 사랑한다.
ko.R: 당신의 향수는 정말 좋은 냄새가 나요. \q 당신의 이름은 쏟아 부은 향긋한 향수 같아요. \q 그래서 젊은 여자들이 당신을 사랑해요.

decisions.choice: oils: scented olive oil rubbed on the skin and hair
decisions.reason: Perfumed oil was a sign of festivity and well-being (Psalm 133:2; Ecclesiastes 9:8; Amos 6:6). She delights in the scent of him.

decisions.choice: your name is oil poured out: who you are spreads like a fragrance
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person and his reputation (Ecclesiastes 7:1 sets a good name beside good oil). When perfume is poured out, its scent fills the room; so does he.

decisions.choice: poured out
decisions.reason: The verb form is unusual and does not match the noun for oil in gender. It is read here as "poured out"; some take it as the name of a kind of oil, "oil of turaq". The image is the same.

decisions.choice: young women: girls old enough to marry
decisions.reason: The word ('alamot) is used of young women of marriageable age (Genesis 24:43; Psalm 68:26; 6:8 below).

decisions.choice: like sweet perfume
decisions.reason: Readable adds "like" so that the comparison is clear.

decisions.choice: "mafuta" (oil) at Literal; "manukato" (perfume) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The oils are scented oils for the skin and hair (m1); Literal keeps "mafuta", and the other levels say what they are to a reader today, "manukato".

source.text: מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ נָּר֑וּצָה הֱבִיאַ֨נִי הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ חֲדָרָ֗יו נָגִ֤ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ נַזְכִּ֤ירָה דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן מֵישָׁרִ֖ים אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Draw me after you, let us run; has brought me the king [into] his chambers; let us rejoice and be glad in you; let us praise your lovemaking more than wine; rightly they love you.

en.L: Draw me after you; let us run! \q The king has brought me into his chambers; let us rejoice and be glad in you; \q let us praise your lovemaking more than wine. \q Rightly they love you.
en.B: Take me with you; let us run! \q The king has brought me into his rooms. We will rejoice and delight in you; \q we will celebrate your love more than wine. \q How right they are to love you!
en.R: Take me with you! Let us hurry! \q The king has taken me into his rooms. We will be glad and happy because of you. \q We will praise your love more than wine. \q No wonder they love you!

es.L: Llévame tras de ti; ¡corramos! \q El rey me ha traído a sus aposentos; gocémonos y alegrémonos en ti; \q celebremos tus caricias más que el vino. \q Rectamente te aman.
es.B: Llévame contigo; ¡corramos! \q El rey me ha llevado a sus habitaciones. Nos alegraremos y nos deleitaremos en ti; \q celebraremos tu amor más que el vino. \q ¡Qué razón tienen al amarte!
es.R: ¡Llévame contigo! ¡Démonos prisa! \q El rey me ha llevado a sus habitaciones. Estaremos alegres y felices gracias a ti. \q Alabaremos tu amor más que el vino. \q ¡No es raro que te amen!

fr.L: Tire-moi après toi ; courons ! \q Le roi m’a fait entrer dans ses chambres ; exultons et réjouissons-nous en toi ; \q célébrons tes caresses plus que le vin. \q C’est avec droiture qu’on t’aime.
fr.B: Emmène-moi avec toi ; courons ! \q Le roi m’a fait entrer dans ses appartements. Nous exulterons et nous nous réjouirons en toi ; \q nous célébrerons ton amour plus que le vin. \q Comme on a raison de t’aimer !
fr.R: Emmène-moi avec toi ! Dépêchons-nous ! \q Le roi m’a fait entrer dans ses chambres. Nous serons dans la joie grâce à toi. \q Nous chanterons ton amour plus que le vin. \q Pas étonnant qu’on t’aime !

sw.L: Univute nyuma yako; na tukimbie! \q Mfalme ameniingiza vyumbani mwake; na tushangilie na kufurahi ndani yako; \q na tuyasifu mahaba yako kuliko divai. \q Kwa haki wanakupenda.
sw.B: Unichukue pamoja nawe; tukimbie! \q Mfalme ameniingiza katika vyumba vyake. Tutashangilia na kufurahi ndani yako; \q tutayasifu mapenzi yako kuliko divai. \q Wana haki kabisa kukupenda!
sw.R: Unichukue pamoja nawe! Twende haraka! \q Mfalme amenipeleka vyumbani mwake. Tutakuwa na furaha na shangwe kwa sababu yako. \q Tutayasifu mapenzi yako kuliko divai. \q Si ajabu wanakupenda!

vi.L: Xin kéo em theo sau anh; chúng ta hãy chạy! \q Vua đã đưa em vào các phòng riêng của chàng; chúng em hãy vui mừng và hân hoan trong anh; \q hãy ca ngợi ân ái của anh hơn rượu. \q Họ yêu anh là chính đáng.
vi.B: Hãy đưa em theo anh; chúng ta cùng chạy! \q Vua đã đưa em vào phòng của chàng. Chúng em sẽ vui mừng và hân hoan nơi anh; \q chúng em sẽ ca tụng tình yêu của anh hơn rượu. \q Họ yêu anh thật là phải lẽ!
vi.R: Hãy đưa em đi với anh! Mình mau đi thôi! \q Vua đã đưa em vào phòng của chàng. Chúng em sẽ vui mừng hạnh phúc vì anh. \q Chúng em sẽ khen ngợi tình yêu của anh hơn rượu. \q Chẳng lạ gì họ yêu anh!

ko.L: 그대 뒤로 나를 이끌어 다오. 우리 달려가자! \q 왕이 나를 그의 방들로 데려왔다. 우리가 그대 안에서 기뻐하고 즐거워하자. \q 그대의 사랑을 포도주보다 더 기리자. \q 그들이 그대를 사랑함이 마땅하다.
ko.B: 나를 데리고 가 다오. 우리 함께 달려가자! \q 왕이 나를 그의 방으로 데려왔다. 우리는 그대로 인해 기뻐하고 즐거워할 것이다. \q 포도주보다 그대의 사랑을 더 기릴 것이다. \q 그들이 그대를 사랑하는 것은 참으로 옳다!
ko.R: 나를 데려가 주세요! 어서 가요! \q 왕이 나를 그의 방으로 데려갔어요. 우리는 당신 때문에 기쁘고 즐거울 거예요. \q 포도주보다 당신의 사랑을 더 칭찬할 거예요. \q 사람들이 당신을 사랑하는 것도 당연해요!

decisions.choice: we will rejoice in you: the young women may speak here, or the woman for herself and others
alternatives: the woman goes on speaking, with others
the young women speak to the woman
decisions.reason: The voice changes from "me" to "we", and the "you" in "rejoice in you" has a form that can be read as feminine. If so, the young women of 1:3 rejoice in her, and then turn to praise his love. The same form can also be a masculine "you" as it is said at a pause, and then the woman still speaks, joined by others. The forms do not settle it.

decisions.choice: the king: what she calls her beloved
decisions.reason: She calls him "the king", here and in 1:12; elsewhere he is a shepherd (1:7; 2:16). Lovers have often spoken of each other as king and queen, and the Song may use the title as a love name; it may also have Solomon in view (1:1; 3:11). The words leave it open.

decisions.choice: chambers: the inner rooms of a house
decisions.reason: The word is used of a private inner room, a bedroom (Genesis 43:30; 2 Samuel 13:10).

decisions.choice: rightly: sincerely, with good reason
decisions.reason: The word (mesharim) means what is upright or straight; here it says that the young women are right to love him. In 7:10 it is used of wine that flows smoothly.

decisions.choice: We will be glad ... we will praise
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the forms that mean "let us" as resolve ("we will"); Literal keeps "let us".

decisions.choice: "Rectamente te aman"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word for what is upright (mesharim, m4) as an adverb; Balanced and Readable say what it means, that they are right to love him.

decisions.choice: "on t'aime" for "they love you"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they" is not tied to a group here; the young women of 1:3 are the likely ones, but "elles" would decide it, while "on" says, as the Hebrew does, that he is loved with good reason.

decisions.choice: "chúng em ... anh": the woman, with the young women, speaks to him
alternatives: "chúng tôi ... chị": the young women speak to her
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose who "we" and "you" are (m1). The draft follows the reading in which the woman speaks for herself and the others to her beloved, so the "you" stays "anh" through the verse; if the young women speak to her, the words would be "chúng tôi" and "chị". "Let us run" is the two lovers, "chúng ta" ("mình" at Readable).

source.text: שְׁחוֹרָ֤ה אֲנִי֙ וְֽנָאוָ֔ה בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כְּאָהֳלֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר כִּירִיע֖וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Black [am] I and lovely, daughters of Jerusalem, like [the] tents of Kedar, like [the] curtains of Solomon.

en.L: Black [am] I and lovely, \q daughters of Jerusalem, \q like [the] tents of Kedar, \q like [the] hangings of Solomon.
en.B: I am dark and lovely, \q women of Jerusalem, \q like the tents of Kedar, \q like Solomon's curtains.
en.R: Women of Jerusalem, my skin is dark, and I am beautiful. \q I am like the tents of Kedar, \q like the curtains of Solomon.

es.L: Negra [soy] yo, y hermosa, \q hijas de Jerusalén, \q como [las] tiendas de Cedar, \q como [las] cortinas de Salomón.
es.B: Soy morena y bella, \q mujeres de Jerusalén, \q como las tiendas de Cedar, \q como las cortinas de Salomón.
es.R: Mujeres de Jerusalén, mi piel es oscura, y soy hermosa. \q Soy como las tiendas de Cedar, \q como las cortinas de Salomón.

fr.L: Noire [suis]-je, et belle, \q filles de Jérusalem, \q comme [les] tentes de Kédar, \q comme [les] tentures de Salomon.
fr.B: Je suis brune et belle, \q femmes de Jérusalem, \q comme les tentes de Kédar, \q comme les tentures de Salomon.
fr.R: Femmes de Jérusalem, j’ai la peau foncée, et je suis belle. \q Je ressemble aux tentes de Kédar, \q aux tentures de Salomon.

sw.L: Mweusi [ni] mimi, na mzuri, \q enyi binti za Yerusalemu, \q kama hema za Kedari, \q kama mapazia ya Sulemani.
sw.B: Mimi ni mweusi na mrembo, \q enyi wanawake wa Yerusalemu, \q kama hema za Kedari, \q kama mapazia ya Sulemani.
sw.R: Wanawake wa Yerusalemu, ngozi yangu ni nyeusi, nami ni mrembo. \q Ninafanana na hema za Kedari, \q na mapazia ya Sulemani.

vi.L: Đen [là] tôi, và xinh đẹp, \q hỡi các con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q như [những] trại của Kê-đa, \q như [những] màn trướng của Sa-lô-môn.
vi.B: Tôi ngăm đen và xinh đẹp, \q hỡi các thiếu nữ Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q như các trại của Kê-đa, \q như các bức màn của Sa-lô-môn.
vi.R: Hỡi các thiếu nữ Giê-ru-sa-lem, da tôi ngăm đen, và tôi xinh đẹp. \q Tôi giống như những chiếc lều của Kê-đa, \q như những bức màn của Sa-lô-môn.

ko.L: 나는 검고 아름답다, \q 예루살렘의 딸들아, \q 게달의 장막들처럼, \q 솔로몬의 휘장들처럼.
ko.B: 나는 가무잡잡하고 아름답다, \q 예루살렘 여인들아, \q 게달의 장막처럼, \q 솔로몬의 휘장처럼.
ko.R: 예루살렘 여인들아, 내 피부는 검고, 나는 아름답다. \q 나는 게달의 장막 같고, \q 솔로몬의 휘장 같다.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks to the women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "Black" and "lovely" are feminine and she says "I"; she addresses a group of women.

decisions.choice: and lovely: the word may also mean "but"
decisions.reason: The joining word (we-) can mean "and" or "but". She may say "I am dark, yet lovely", answering the stares of 1:6, or "I am dark and lovely", the two belonging together. The translation keeps "and", which allows both.

decisions.choice: daughters of Jerusalem: the women of the city
decisions.reason: "Daughters of" a city means the women who live there (Isaiah 3:16). These women are the woman's companions and listeners in the Song (2:7; 3:5, 10-11; 5:8, 16; 8:4).

decisions.choice: the tents of Kedar ... the curtains of Solomon: dark, and also fine
decisions.reason: Kedar was a tribe of nomads in the desert east of Israel (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16-17; Psalm 120:5), whose tents were woven of black goat hair. Solomon's curtains were costly hangings, of a royal tent or palace. The two pictures match "black" and "lovely".

decisions.choice: women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "women" for "daughters", the sense of the phrase (m3); Literal keeps "daughters".

decisions.choice: dark
decisions.reason: "Black" in Literal; Balanced and Readable say "dark", since she speaks of skin darkened by the sun (1:6).

decisions.choice: "mweusi" (black) at every level, "ngozi yangu ni nyeusi" at Readable
decisions.reason: Swahili "maji ya kunde" names a light brown skin and would soften the contrast she draws with the black tents of Kedar; "mweusi" keeps it, and 1:6 says the sun made her so.

decisions.choice: "các con gái Giê-ru-sa-lem" (L); "các thiếu nữ Giê-ru-sa-lem" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: Literal keeps "daughters"; Balanced and Readable say "thiếu nữ", young women, the women of the city who are her companions (m3). The woman says "tôi" to them, not "em", which she keeps for her beloved.

decisions.choice: "예루살렘의 딸들아" (L); "예루살렘 여인들아" (B, R), in 해라체
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: the woman speaks to the women of the city as to companions, in the plain 해라체 with the vocative -아; they answer her the same way.

source.text: אַל־תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת שֶׁשֱּׁזָפַ֖תְנִי הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י נִֽחֲרוּ־בִ֗י שָׂמֻ֨נִי֙ נֹטֵרָ֣ה אֶת־הַכְּרָמִ֔ים כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לֹ֥א נָטָֽרְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not look at me that I [am] darkened, that has looked on me the sun; [the] sons of my mother were angry with me; they made me keeper of the vineyards; my vineyard, which [is] mine, I have not kept.

en.L: Do not stare at me because I [am] darkened, \q because the sun has looked on me. \q The sons of my mother were angry with me; they made me keeper of the vineyards; \q my vineyard, my own, I have not kept.
en.B: Do not stare at me because I am so dark, \q because the sun has looked down on me. \q My mother's sons were angry with me and made me look after the vineyards; \q my own vineyard I have not looked after.
en.R: Do not stare at me because my skin is dark. \q The sun has tanned me. \q My brothers were angry with me. They made me take care of the vineyards. \q But I have not taken care of my own vineyard.

es.L: No {{plural_you:me miren|me miréis}} porque yo [estoy] ennegrecida, \q porque el sol me ha mirado. \q Los hijos de mi madre se enojaron conmigo; me pusieron [como] guardiana de las viñas; \q mi viña, la mía, no [la] he guardado.
es.B: No {{plural_you:me miren|me miréis}} fijamente por ser tan morena, \q porque el sol me ha mirado desde lo alto. \q Los hijos de mi madre se enojaron conmigo y me pusieron a cuidar las viñas; \q mi propia viña no la he cuidado.
es.R: No {{plural_you:me miren|me miréis}} así porque mi piel es oscura. \q El sol me ha bronceado. \q Mis hermanos se enojaron conmigo. Me pusieron a cuidar las viñas. \q Pero no he cuidado mi propia viña.

fr.L: Ne me regardez pas parce que je [suis] noircie, \q parce que le soleil m’a regardée. \q Les fils de ma mère se sont fâchés contre moi ; ils m’ont établie gardienne des vignes ; \q ma vigne, celle qui est à moi, je ne l’ai pas gardée.
fr.B: Ne me dévisagez pas parce que je suis si brune, \q parce que le soleil a posé son regard sur moi. \q Les fils de ma mère se sont fâchés contre moi et m’ont chargée de garder les vignes ; \q ma propre vigne, je ne l’ai pas gardée.
fr.R: Ne me regardez pas comme ça parce que j’ai la peau foncée. \q C’est le soleil qui m’a bronzée. \q Mes frères étaient en colère contre moi. Ils m’ont obligée à m’occuper des vignes. \q Mais ma propre vigne, je ne m’en suis pas occupée.

sw.L: Msinitazame kwa kuwa mimi [ni] mweusi, \q kwa kuwa jua limenitazama. \q Wana wa mama yangu walinikasirikia; walinifanya mlinzi wa mashamba ya mizabibu; \q shamba langu la mizabibu, langu mwenyewe, sikulilinda.
sw.B: Msinikodolee macho kwa sababu mimi ni mweusi sana, \q kwa sababu jua limeniangalia kutoka juu. \q Wana wa mama yangu walinikasirikia, wakanifanya niyatunze mashamba ya mizabibu; \q shamba langu mwenyewe la mizabibu sikulitunza.
sw.R: Msinikodolee macho kwa sababu ngozi yangu ni nyeusi. \q Jua limeniunguza. \q Kaka zangu walinikasirikia. Walinilazimisha kutunza mashamba ya mizabibu. \q Lakini shamba langu mwenyewe sikulitunza.

vi.L: [Các chị] đừng nhìn tôi vì tôi [bị] đen sạm, \q vì mặt trời đã nhìn tôi. \q Các con trai của mẹ tôi đã giận tôi; họ bắt tôi làm người giữ các vườn nho; \q vườn nho của tôi, của riêng tôi, tôi đã không giữ.
vi.B: Các chị đừng nhìn chằm chằm vào tôi vì tôi đen sạm, \q vì mặt trời đã nhìn xuống tôi. \q Các con trai của mẹ tôi giận tôi và bắt tôi trông coi các vườn nho; \q còn vườn nho của riêng tôi, tôi lại chẳng trông coi.
vi.R: Các chị đừng nhìn tôi chằm chằm vì da tôi đen. \q Nắng đã làm da tôi sạm đi. \q Các anh tôi giận tôi. Họ bắt tôi chăm sóc các vườn nho. \q Nhưng vườn nho của chính tôi, tôi lại không chăm sóc.

ko.L: 내가 거무스름하다고 나를 쳐다보지 마라, \q 해가 나를 바라보았기 때문이다. \q 내 어머니의 아들들이 내게 화를 내어 나를 포도원들을 지키는 자로 삼았다. \q 나의 포도원, 내 것은 내가 지키지 않았다.
ko.B: 내가 너무 검다고 나를 빤히 쳐다보지 마라, \q 햇볕이 나를 내리쬐었기 때문이다. \q 내 어머니의 아들들이 내게 화가 나서 나에게 포도원을 돌보게 했다. \q 정작 내 포도원은 내가 돌보지 못했다.
ko.R: 내 피부가 검다고 그렇게 쳐다보지 마라. \q 햇볕에 그을렸을 뿐이다. \q 내 오빠들이 내게 화가 나서 나에게 포도원을 돌보게 했다. \q 그래서 내 포도원은 돌보지 못했다.

decisions.choice: darkened by the sun: from working outdoors
decisions.reason: Her skin is dark because she has worked in the vineyards in the sun. A pale skin could mark someone who did not have to work outside, so the women of the city stare.

decisions.choice: darkened
decisions.reason: The word repeats part of the word "black" (1:5). The repetition may make it milder ("darkish") or stronger ("very dark").

decisions.choice: my mother's sons: her brothers
decisions.reason: She speaks of her mother's household and never of a father (3:4; 8:2). Brothers had a say in a sister's life and marriage (Genesis 24:50, 55; 34:11-13); compare 8:8-9.

decisions.choice: my own vineyard: herself
decisions.reason: The vineyard is an image she uses for herself, her body and her love (2:15; 8:12). While she guarded her brothers' vineyards, she had no time to care for her own: her looks, or her own life and love.

decisions.choice: The sun has tanned me; My brothers
alternatives: the sun has looked on me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sun's gaze did and calls her mother's sons her brothers (m1, m3).

decisions.choice: "{{plural_you:me miren|me miréis}}"
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: wherever a group is addressed (the women of Jerusalem, the friends of 5:1), the verb and pronoun take the plural_you setting, with the Latin American form first and the form of Spain as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "[Các chị]"
decisions.reason: A Vietnamese command does not show that several people are addressed, which the Hebrew verb does; Literal supplies "các chị" in brackets, and Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: "내 오빠들"
decisions.reason: Readable calls her mother's sons her brothers, as the English Readable does (m3); a woman's brothers are "오빠" in Korean (or "남동생" if younger); the older word suits brothers who had a say over her.

source.text: הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֵיכָ֣ה תִרְעֶ֔ה אֵיכָ֖ה תַּרְבִּ֣יץ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם שַׁלָּמָ֤ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ כְּעֹ֣טְיָ֔ה עַ֖ל עֶדְרֵ֥י חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Tell me, [you] whom my soul loves, where do you pasture, where do you make lie down at noon; for why should I be like one veiled beside [the] flocks of your companions?

en.L: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, \q where do you pasture [your flock]? \q Where do you make [it] lie down at noon? \q For why should I be like one who veils herself \q beside the flocks of your companions?
en.B: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, \q where do you graze your flock? \q Where do you let it rest at noon? \q Why should I be like a woman wearing a veil \q beside the flocks of your companions?
en.R: Tell me, you whom I love with all my heart, \q where are you taking your sheep and goats to eat? \q Where do you let them rest at noon? \q Why should I be like a woman with a veil, \q looking for you among the flocks of your friends?

es.L: Dime, tú a quien ama mi alma, \q ¿dónde apacientas [tu rebaño]? \q ¿Dónde [lo] haces reposar al mediodía? \q Pues ¿por qué he de ser como una que se cubre con un velo \q junto a los rebaños de tus compañeros?
es.B: Dime, tú a quien ama mi alma, \q ¿dónde llevas a pastar tu rebaño? \q ¿Dónde lo haces descansar al mediodía? \q ¿Por qué he de ser como una mujer cubierta con un velo \q junto a los rebaños de tus compañeros?
es.R: Dime, tú, a quien amo con todo mi corazón, \q ¿adónde llevas a comer a tus ovejas y cabras? \q ¿Dónde las dejas descansar al mediodía? \q ¿Por qué tendría que andar como una mujer con velo, \q buscándote entre los rebaños de tus amigos?

fr.L: Dis-moi, toi qu’aime mon âme, \q où fais-tu paître [ton troupeau] ? \q Où [le] fais-tu reposer à midi ? \q Car pourquoi serais-je comme une femme qui se voile \q auprès des troupeaux de tes compagnons ?
fr.B: Dis-moi, toi que mon âme aime, \q où mènes-tu paître ton troupeau ? \q Où le laisses-tu se reposer à midi ? \q Pourquoi devrais-je être comme une femme voilée \q près des troupeaux de tes compagnons ?
fr.R: Dis-moi, toi que j’aime de tout mon cœur, \q où emmènes-tu manger tes moutons et tes chèvres ? \q Où les laisses-tu se reposer à midi ? \q Pourquoi devrais-je être comme une femme voilée \q qui te cherche parmi les troupeaux de tes amis ?

sw.L: Niambie, wewe ambaye nafsi yangu inakupenda, \q unalisha [kundi lako] wapi? \q Unalilaza wapi adhuhuri? \q Kwa maana kwa nini niwe kama mwanamke ajifunikaye \q karibu na makundi ya wenzako?
sw.B: Niambie, wewe ambaye nafsi yangu inakupenda, \q unalichunga kundi lako wapi? \q Unaliacha lipumzike wapi wakati wa adhuhuri? \q Kwa nini niwe kama mwanamke aliyejitanda shela \q karibu na makundi ya wenzako?
sw.R: Niambie, wewe ninayekupenda kwa moyo wangu wote, \q unawapeleka wapi kondoo na mbuzi wako kula? \q Unawaacha wapumzike wapi mchana? \q Kwa nini niwe kama mwanamke aliyejifunika uso, \q nikikutafuta kati ya makundi ya rafiki zako?

vi.L: Hãy nói cho em biết, hỡi người mà linh hồn em yêu, \q anh chăn [bầy] ở đâu? \q Anh cho [bầy] nằm nghỉ ở đâu lúc giữa trưa? \q Vì sao em phải như người đàn bà trùm khăn \q bên cạnh các bầy của bạn bè anh?
vi.B: Hãy cho em biết, hỡi người mà linh hồn em yêu mến, \q anh chăn bầy ở đâu? \q Giữa trưa anh cho bầy nghỉ ở đâu? \q Sao em phải như người phụ nữ che mạng \q bên các bầy của bạn bè anh?
vi.R: Hãy nói cho em biết, anh, người em yêu hết lòng, \q anh dẫn chiên dê đi ăn ở đâu? \q Giữa trưa anh cho chúng nghỉ ở đâu? \q Sao em phải như một người phụ nữ che mặt, \q đi tìm anh giữa các bầy của bạn bè anh?

ko.L: 내 영혼이 사랑하는 그대여, 내게 말해 다오. \q 그대는 어디서 [양 떼를] 먹이는가? \q 한낮에 어디서 [양 떼를] 쉬게 하는가? \q 어찌하여 내가 얼굴을 가린 여자처럼 되어 \q 그대 동료들의 양 떼 곁에 있어야 하는가?
ko.B: 내 영혼이 사랑하는 그대여, 말해 다오. \q 그대는 어디서 양 떼를 먹이는가? \q 한낮에는 어디서 양 떼를 쉬게 하는가? \q 왜 내가 너울을 쓴 여자처럼 \q 그대 동료들의 양 떼 곁에 있어야 하는가?
ko.R: 내가 온 마음으로 사랑하는 당신, 말해 주세요. \q 양과 염소를 어디로 데려가 먹이나요? \q 한낮에는 어디서 쉬게 하나요? \q 왜 내가 너울을 쓴 여자처럼 \q 당신 친구들의 양 떼 사이에서 당신을 찾아다녀야 하나요?

decisions.choice: she speaks to him
decisions.reason: The verbs and "your" are masculine: the woman now speaks to her beloved.

decisions.choice: you whom my soul loves: the one I love with all that I am
decisions.reason: The "soul" (nefesh) is the whole living self, with its desires. The phrase is her name for him again in 3:1-4.

decisions.choice: where do you pasture ... at noon: he is pictured as a shepherd
decisions.reason: At midday shepherds led their flocks to shade and water to rest (Psalm 23:2; Jeremiah 33:12). She wants to know where to find him.

decisions.choice: like one who veils herself: a woman whose veil would be misread
decisions.reason: The word means one who covers or wraps herself. A woman veiled and alone among shepherds might be taken for a prostitute (Genesis 38:14-15), or for a woman in mourning. Some ancient versions read a word with one letter changed: "like one who wanders".

decisions.choice: looking for you among the flocks
decisions.reason: Readable says why she would be among the flocks; the Hebrew implies it.

decisions.choice: you whom I love with all my heart
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my soul loves" means in everyday English (m2).

decisions.choice: "얼굴을 가린 여자처럼 되어 \q 그대 동료들의 양 떼 곁에"
alternatives: keeping "beside the flocks" on the first of the two lines
decisions.reason: Korean puts the place before the verb, so the two lines are built so that each still holds the Hebrew line's own words: first the veiled woman, then the flocks of his companions.

source.text: אִם־לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ לָ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים צְֽאִי־לָ֞ךְ בְּעִקְבֵ֣י הַצֹּ֗אן וּרְעִי֙ אֶת־גְּדִיֹּתַ֔יִךְ עַ֖ל מִשְׁכְּנ֥וֹת הָרֹעִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: If you do not know for yourself, the most beautiful among women, go out for yourself in [the] tracks of the flock and pasture your young goats beside [the] tents of the shepherds.

en.L: If you do not know for yourself, \q most beautiful among women, \q go out in the tracks of the flock, \q and pasture your young goats beside the tents of the shepherds.
en.B: If you do not know, \q most beautiful of women, \q go out and follow the flock's tracks, \q and graze your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
en.R: Most beautiful of women, if you do not know, \q follow the tracks of the flock. \q Feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.

es.L: Si no [lo] sabes tú, \q la más hermosa entre las mujeres, \q sal tras las huellas del rebaño \q y pastorea tus cabritos junto a las tiendas de los pastores.
es.B: Si no lo sabes, \q tú, la más hermosa de las mujeres, \q sal y sigue las huellas del rebaño, \q y lleva a pastar tus cabritos junto a las tiendas de los pastores.
es.R: Mujer más hermosa que ninguna, si no lo sabes, \q sigue las huellas del rebaño. \q Lleva a comer a tus cabritos cerca de las tiendas de los pastores.

fr.L: Si tu ne [le] sais pas toi-même, \q toi la plus belle parmi les femmes, \q va-t’en sur la piste du troupeau, \q et mène paître tes chevrettes auprès des tentes des bergers.
fr.B: Si tu ne le sais pas, \q toi, la plus belle de toutes les femmes, \q sors et suis la piste du troupeau, \q et fais brouter tes chevreaux près des tentes des bergers.
fr.R: Toi, la plus belle des femmes, si tu ne le sais pas, \q suis les traces du troupeau. \q Fais manger tes chevreaux près des tentes des bergers.

sw.L: Usipojua mwenyewe, \q ewe mrembo kuliko wanawake wote, \q nenda nje kwenye alama za miguu ya kundi, \q na uwachunge mbuzi wako wadogo kando ya makao ya wachungaji.
sw.B: Kama hujui, \q ewe mrembo kuliko wanawake wote, \q toka ukafuate alama za nyayo za kundi, \q uwalishe mbuzi wako wadogo karibu na mahema ya wachungaji.
sw.R: Ewe mrembo kuliko wanawake wote, kama hujui, \q fuata alama za nyayo za kundi. \q Walishe mbuzi wako wadogo karibu na mahema ya wachungaji.

vi.L: Nếu em không biết, \q hỡi người đẹp nhất giữa các phụ nữ, \q hãy ra đi theo dấu chân của bầy, \q và chăn dê con của em bên cạnh các lều của những người chăn.
vi.B: Nếu em không biết, \q hỡi người đẹp nhất trong các phụ nữ, \q hãy ra đi theo dấu chân bầy chiên, \q và chăn đàn dê con của em gần lều những người chăn.
vi.R: Hỡi người đẹp nhất trong mọi phụ nữ, nếu em không biết, \q hãy đi theo dấu chân của bầy. \q Hãy cho đàn dê con của em ăn gần lều của những người chăn.

ko.L: 만일 그대가 알지 못하거든, \q 여인들 가운데 가장 아름다운 이여, \q 양 떼의 발자취를 따라 나가서, \q 목자들의 장막 곁에서 그대의 어린 염소들을 먹여라.
ko.B: 그대가 모른다면, \q 여인들 가운데 가장 아름다운 이여, \q 나가서 양 떼의 발자국을 따라가, \q 목자들의 장막 곁에서 그대의 새끼 염소들을 먹여라.
ko.R: 여자들 가운데 가장 아름다운 당신, 모른다면 \q 양 떼의 발자국을 따라가세요. \q 목자들의 천막 근처에서 당신의 새끼 염소들을 먹이세요.

decisions.choice: an answer to the woman: from the man, or from the women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verbs are feminine singular: someone speaks to the woman. The man may answer her question of 1:7, teasing her to find him among the shepherds. The women of Jerusalem also call her "most beautiful among women" (5:9; 6:1), and they may be the ones who answer.

decisions.choice: for yourself
decisions.reason: The little phrase "for yourself" after a verb adds emphasis, a personal touch (Genesis 12:1, "go for yourself"). It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: your young goats ... the shepherds' tents: she, too, keeps a flock
decisions.reason: She is pictured as a shepherd girl with her own young goats; following the tracks of the flock she will come to the tents where the shepherds rest.

decisions.choice: "va-t'en" for "go out for yourself"
decisions.reason: French "s'en aller" carries the personal touch of the Hebrew "for yourself" (m2) without adding words; Balanced and Readable say simply "sors" or "suis".

decisions.choice: "em" for the woman addressed
decisions.reason: Whether the man or the women of Jerusalem answer her (m1), both would call her "em", so the Vietnamese can leave the speaker open, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: the man answers her, in 해요체 with "당신"
alternatives: the women of Jerusalem answer, in 해라체 ("…따라가라")
decisions.reason: Korean must choose a speech level, and so a speaker (m1). Readable follows the reading that the man answers her question of 1:7; Literal and Balanced use "그대" and the plain style, which fit either speaker.

records.literal_gloss: To a mare among [the] chariots of Pharaoh I liken you, my companion.

en.L: To a mare among the chariots of Pharaoh \q I liken you, my companion.
en.B: I compare you, my darling, \q to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
en.R: My darling, you are like a mare \q among the chariot horses of Pharaoh.

es.L: A una yegua entre los carros del faraón \q te comparo, compañera mía.
es.B: Te comparo, amada mía, \q con una yegua entre los carros del faraón.
es.R: Amada mía, eres como una yegua \q entre los caballos de los carros del faraón.

fr.L: À une jument parmi les chars de Pharaon \q je te compare, ma compagne.
fr.B: Je te compare, ma bien-aimée, \q à une jument parmi les chars de Pharaon.
fr.R: Ma bien-aimée, tu es comme une jument \q parmi les chevaux des chars de Pharaon.

sw.L: Kwa farasi jike kati ya magari ya vita ya Farao \q nimekufananisha, rafiki yangu.
sw.B: Nakufananisha, mpenzi wangu, \q na farasi jike kati ya magari ya vita ya Farao.
sw.R: Mpenzi wangu, wewe ni kama farasi jike \q kati ya farasi wa magari ya vita ya Farao.

vi.L: Với con ngựa cái giữa các chiến xa của Pha-ra-ôn \q anh ví em, bạn lòng của anh.
vi.B: Anh ví em, em yêu dấu, \q như con ngựa cái giữa các chiến xa của Pha-ra-ôn.
vi.R: Em yêu, em như con ngựa cái \q giữa đàn ngựa kéo chiến xa của Pha-ra-ôn.

ko.L: 바로의 병거들 가운데 있는 암말에 \q 나의 짝이여, 내가 그대를 견준다.
ko.B: 나의 연인이여, 나는 그대를 \q 바로의 병거들 사이에 있는 암말에 견준다.
ko.R: 내 연인, 당신은 \q 바로의 병거를 끄는 말들 가운데 있는 암말 같아요.

decisions.choice: the man speaks to the woman (1:9-11)
decisions.reason: "You" and "my companion" are feminine, and the one who speaks calls her his: the man now speaks.

decisions.choice: my companion: the man's word for her
decisions.reason: The word (ra'yah) is the feminine of the word for a friend or neighbor: one who is close, a dear companion. It is his word for her nine times in the Song.

decisions.choice: a mare among Pharaoh's chariots: splendid, and impossible to ignore
decisions.reason: Egypt's chariots were famous, and Solomon bought horses and chariots from Egypt (1 Kings 10:28-29). The chariot horses were stallions; a mare among them would set them all astir. She is as splendid as a royal horse in its harness (1:10), and she draws every eye.

decisions.choice: my darling
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "my darling" for the man's word for her (m2); Literal keeps "my companion", which shows the sense of friendship in the word.

decisions.choice: "compañera mía" (L); "amada mía" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: the man's word for her (m2) is a close companion; Literal shows that with "compañera mía", and Balanced and Readable say what it is in a love song, "amada mía". "Amiga mía" sounds like mere friendship in modern Spanish.

decisions.choice: "ma compagne" (L); "ma bien-aimée" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: the man's word for her (m2) is a dear companion; Literal says "ma compagne", and Balanced and Readable "ma bien-aimée", what it means between lovers. "Mon amie" now reads as friendship or as a girlfriend.

decisions.choice: "rafiki yangu" (L); "mpenzi wangu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: Literal keeps the sense of a close friend (m2); Balanced and Readable say "mpenzi wangu", his word for her, while "mpendwa wangu" is kept for her word for him (dodi), so the address word shows who speaks.

decisions.choice: "bạn lòng của anh" (L); "em yêu dấu" (B); "em yêu" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: "bạn lòng" keeps the friendship in the man's word for her (m2) at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the address a man gives the woman he loves.

decisions.choice: "나의 짝이여" (L); "나의 연인이여" (B); "내 연인" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: "짝" keeps the sense of a close companion (m2); "연인" says she is his beloved. "사랑" is kept for her word for him (내 사랑, dodi), so the address word shows who speaks.

records.literal_gloss: Lovely [are] your cheeks with ornaments, your neck with strings of beads.

en.L: Lovely [are] your cheeks with ornaments, \q your neck with strings of beads.
en.B: Your cheeks are lovely between the ornaments, \q your neck with its strings of beads.
en.R: Your face is beautiful with jewelry beside it, \q and your neck with strings of beads.

es.L: Hermosas [son] tus mejillas con adornos, \q tu cuello con hilos de cuentas.
es.B: Tus mejillas son hermosas entre los adornos, \q y tu cuello con sus hilos de cuentas.
es.R: Tu rostro es hermoso con las joyas que lo adornan, \q y tu cuello con sus collares de cuentas.

fr.L: Belles [sont] tes joues avec des pendants, \q ton cou avec des rangs de perles.
fr.B: Tes joues sont belles entre les pendants, \q ton cou avec ses rangs de perles.
fr.R: Ton visage est beau avec les bijoux qui l’encadrent, \q et ton cou avec ses colliers de perles.

sw.L: Mashavu yako [ni] mazuri kwa mapambo, \q shingo yako kwa mikufu ya shanga.
sw.B: Mashavu yako yanapendeza kati ya mapambo, \q shingo yako na mikufu yake ya shanga.
sw.R: Uso wako ni mzuri pamoja na vito vilivyo kando yake, \q na shingo yako pamoja na mikufu ya shanga.

vi.L: Đáng yêu [thay] đôi má em với các đồ trang sức, \q cổ em với những chuỗi hạt.
vi.B: Đôi má em xinh đẹp giữa các đồ trang sức, \q cổ em với những chuỗi hạt.
vi.R: Khuôn mặt em thật đẹp với trang sức hai bên, \q và cổ em với những chuỗi hạt.

ko.L: 장식들로 그대의 뺨이 사랑스럽고, \q 구슬 꿰미들로 그대의 목이 [사랑스럽다].
ko.B: 장식 사이로 그대의 뺨이 사랑스럽고, \q 구슬 목걸이를 건 그대의 목도 사랑스럽다.
ko.R: 장신구로 꾸민 당신의 얼굴이 아름다워요. \q 구슬 목걸이를 건 당신의 목도요.

decisions.choice: ornaments ... strings of beads: jewelry framing her face and neck
decisions.reason: The ornaments may be rings or plaits hanging from a headband beside the cheeks, the way a royal horse wore ornaments on its bridle (1:9; Judges 8:21). The second word appears only here and means strung beads or shells.

source.text: תּוֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ נַעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ עִ֖ם נְקֻדּ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: Ornaments of gold we will make for you, with studs of the silver.

en.L: Ornaments of gold we will make for you, \q with studs of silver.
en.B: We will make you ornaments of gold, \q set with points of silver.
en.R: We will make you gold jewelry \q decorated with silver.

es.L: Adornos de oro haremos para ti, \q con incrustaciones de plata.
es.B: Te haremos adornos de oro \q con puntos de plata.
es.R: Te haremos joyas de oro \q adornadas con plata.

fr.L: Des pendants d’or nous ferons pour toi, \q avec des clous d’argent.
fr.B: Nous te ferons des pendants d’or \q sertis de points d’argent.
fr.R: Nous te ferons des bijoux en or \q décorés d’argent.

sw.L: Mapambo ya dhahabu tutakutengenezea, \q pamoja na vitone vya fedha.
sw.B: Tutakutengenezea mapambo ya dhahabu \q yaliyopambwa kwa vitone vya fedha.
sw.R: Tutakutengenezea vito vya dhahabu \q vilivyopambwa kwa fedha.

vi.L: Đồ trang sức bằng vàng chúng tôi sẽ làm cho em, \q với những hạt bằng bạc.
vi.B: Chúng tôi sẽ làm cho em những đồ trang sức bằng vàng \q đính những hạt bạc.
vi.R: Chúng tôi sẽ làm cho em đồ trang sức bằng vàng \q có trang trí bằng bạc.

ko.L: 금 장식들을 우리가 그대에게 만들어 주겠다, \q 은 점들을 박아서.
ko.B: 우리가 그대에게 금 장식을 만들어 주겠다, \q 은 구슬을 박아서.
ko.R: 우리가 당신에게 금 장신구를 만들어 줄게요. \q 은으로 꾸며서요.

decisions.choice: we will make: the man with others, or the women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The plural may be the man speaking for himself and others, or a group, perhaps the women of Jerusalem, joining in. The forms do not say.

decisions.choice: studs: small points or beads
decisions.reason: The word means dots or points; here small silver beads or studs set into the gold.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" for "we"
decisions.reason: The speakers are not certain (m1): the man with others, or the women of Jerusalem. "Chúng anh" would decide for the man and "chúng chị" for the women; "chúng tôi" leaves it open, as the Hebrew does.

records.literal_gloss: While the king [was] at his couch, my nard gave its fragrance.

en.L: While the king [was] at his couch, \q my nard gave forth its fragrance.
en.B: While the king was on his couch, \q my nard gave off its scent.
en.R: While the king was lying on his couch, \q my perfume of nard filled the air with its sweet smell.

es.L: Mientras el rey [estaba] en su lecho de banquete, \q mi nardo exhaló su fragancia.
es.B: Mientras el rey estaba en su diván, \q mi nardo esparció su aroma.
es.R: Mientras el rey estaba recostado en su diván, \q mi perfume de nardo llenaba el aire con su dulce olor.

fr.L: Tandis que le roi [était] sur son divan, \q mon nard a donné son parfum.
fr.B: Pendant que le roi était sur son divan, \q mon nard répandait son odeur.
fr.R: Pendant que le roi était allongé sur son divan, \q mon parfum de nard remplissait l’air de sa douce odeur.

sw.L: Wakati mfalme [alipokuwa] kwenye kiti chake cha kuegemea, \q nardo yangu ilitoa harufu yake.
sw.B: Mfalme alipokuwa ameegemea mezani pake, \q nardo yangu ilitoa harufu yake nzuri.
sw.R: Mfalme alipokuwa amejilaza kwenye kiti chake, \q manukato yangu ya nardo yalijaza hewa kwa harufu nzuri.

vi.L: Trong khi vua [ở] trên trường kỷ của mình, \q cam tùng của tôi tỏa hương.
vi.B: Khi vua đang ngả mình trên trường kỷ, \q dầu cam tùng của tôi tỏa ngát hương thơm.
vi.R: Khi vua đang nằm trên trường kỷ, \q dầu thơm cam tùng của tôi tỏa hương ngọt ngào khắp nơi.

ko.L: 왕이 자기 침상에 [있는] 동안, \q 나의 나드가 그 향기를 풍겼다.
ko.B: 왕이 잔칫상에 기대어 있는 동안, \q 내 나드 향유가 향기를 풍겼다.
ko.R: 왕이 침상에 누워 있는 동안 \q 내 나드 향유가 달콤한 향기를 가득 풍겼다.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks (1:12-14)
decisions.reason: She speaks of "my nard" and of the king, and in 1:13 of "my beloved".

decisions.choice: his couch: the couch on which he reclines
decisions.reason: The word means something round: the couches set around a table where people reclined at a feast, or the couch itself. It may also mean "his circle", his company.

decisions.choice: nard: a costly perfume
decisions.reason: Nard (spikenard) is a fragrant oil from a plant of the Himalayas, carried to Israel from India and very expensive (4:13-14; Mark 14:3; John 12:3).

decisions.choice: my perfume of nard ... sweet smell
decisions.reason: Readable says that nard is a perfume (m3).

decisions.choice: "tôi" when she speaks of him to others
decisions.reason: In 1:12-14 she speaks about the king, not to him, so she says "tôi" and "người yêu dấu của tôi", as the terms for the Song set; "em" is kept for her words to him.

decisions.choice: plain style ("풍겼다") at Readable
decisions.reason: Readable keeps 해요체 for the lovers speaking to each other; when she speaks of him, as here, the plain style of the poem is used at every level.

source.text: צְר֨וֹר הַמֹּ֤ר׀דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בֵּ֥ין שָׁדַ֖י יָלִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: A bundle of the myrrh [is] my beloved to me; between my breasts he lodges.

en.L: A pouch of myrrh [is] my beloved to me; \q between my breasts he lies [all night].
en.B: My beloved is a pouch of myrrh to me, \q resting all night between my breasts.
en.R: My love is like a little bag of myrrh to me, \q lying between my breasts all night.

es.L: Bolsita de mirra [es] mi amado para mí; \q entre mis pechos pasa [la noche].
es.B: Mi amado es para mí una bolsita de mirra \q que pasa la noche entre mis pechos.
es.R: Mi amor es para mí como una bolsita de mirra \q que descansa entre mis pechos toda la noche.

fr.L: Un sachet de myrrhe [est] mon bien-aimé pour moi ; \q entre mes seins il passe [la nuit].
fr.B: Mon bien-aimé est pour moi un sachet de myrrhe \q qui passe la nuit entre mes seins.
fr.R: Mon amour est pour moi comme un petit sac de myrrhe \q posé entre mes seins toute la nuit.

sw.L: Kifuko cha manemane [ni] mpendwa wangu kwangu; \q kati ya matiti yangu analala [usiku kucha].
sw.B: Mpendwa wangu kwangu ni kifuko cha manemane, \q kinachokaa usiku kucha kati ya matiti yangu.
sw.R: Mpendwa wangu ni kama kifuko kidogo cha manemane kwangu, \q kilicholala kati ya matiti yangu usiku kucha.

vi.L: Một túi mộc dược [là] người yêu dấu của tôi đối với tôi; \q giữa ngực tôi chàng nằm [suốt đêm].
vi.B: Người yêu dấu của tôi là túi mộc dược đối với tôi, \q nằm suốt đêm giữa ngực tôi.
vi.R: Người yêu của tôi như túi mộc dược nhỏ đối với tôi, \q nằm giữa ngực tôi suốt đêm.

ko.L: 나의 사랑하는 이는 내게 몰약 주머니[이다]. \q 내 가슴 사이에서 [밤새] 머문다.
ko.B: 내 사랑하는 이는 내게 몰약 주머니, \q 밤새도록 내 가슴 사이에 머문다.
ko.R: 내 사랑은 내게 작은 몰약 주머니 같아서, \q 밤새도록 내 가슴 사이에 놓여 있다.

decisions.choice: my beloved: the woman's word for the man
decisions.reason: The word (dod) means a loved one, a lover; with "my" it is the woman's name for him, more than twenty-five times in the Song. Its plural is the word for lovemaking (1:2).

decisions.choice: a pouch of myrrh: perfume worn on the body
decisions.reason: Myrrh is a fragrant resin from trees of Arabia and East Africa (Psalm 45:9; Proverbs 7:17). Women wore it in a small bag hung from the neck, where it rested between the breasts and scented the body.

decisions.choice: he lies: the pouch, and so the beloved
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay the night. Its subject can be the pouch or the beloved, since both words are masculine; the picture joins them: he is as close to her as the perfume she wears.

decisions.choice: My love
decisions.reason: Readable says "my love" for her word for him (m1); Literal and Balanced say "my beloved".

decisions.choice: all night
decisions.reason: The verb itself means to spend the night (Genesis 19:2); English needs the words.

decisions.choice: "mi amado" (L, B); "mi amor" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: her word for him (dod, m1) is "mi amado", and Readable says "mi amor", as the English does; "amada mía" is his word for her, so the address shows who speaks.

decisions.choice: "mon bien-aimé" (L, B); "mon amour" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: her word for him (m1). French agreement keeps "mon bien-aimé" apart from his "ma bien-aimée" for her, so the words show who speaks.

decisions.choice: "mpendwa wangu" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: her word for him (m1) is "mpendwa wangu", the one I love, and his word for her is "mpenzi wangu", so that Swahili, which has no gender in its verbs, still shows who speaks.

decisions.choice: "người yêu dấu của tôi" (L, B), "người yêu của tôi" (R) when she speaks of him; to him "người yêu dấu của em" (L, B), "anh yêu" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: her word for him (m1) takes the pronoun of the person she speaks to, "tôi" before others and "em" before him.

decisions.choice: "나의 사랑하는 이" (L); "내 사랑하는 이" (B); "내 사랑" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole Song: her word for him (m1); "사랑하는 이" says "the one I love" without the gender Korean pronouns lack, and keeps apart from his words for her, "짝" and "연인".

source.text: אֶשְׁכֹּ֨ל הַכֹּ֤פֶר׀דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בְּכַרְמֵ֖י עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: A cluster of the henna [is] my beloved to me in [the] vineyards of En-gedi.

en.L: A cluster of henna blossoms [is] my beloved to me \q in the vineyards of En-gedi.
en.B: My beloved is a cluster of henna blossoms for me \q in the vineyards of En-gedi.
en.R: My love is like a bunch of henna flowers to me \q in the vineyards of En-gedi.

es.L: Ramillete de alheña [es] mi amado para mí \q en los viñedos de En-gadi.
es.B: Mi amado es para mí un ramillete de flores de alheña \q en los viñedos de En-gadi.
es.R: Mi amor es para mí como un ramo de flores de alheña \q en los viñedos de En-gadi.

fr.L: Une grappe de henné [est] mon bien-aimé pour moi \q dans les vignes d’En-Guédi.
fr.B: Mon bien-aimé est pour moi une grappe de fleurs de henné \q dans les vignes d’En-Guédi.
fr.R: Mon amour est pour moi comme un bouquet de fleurs de henné \q dans les vignes d’En-Guédi.

sw.L: Kishada cha maua ya hina [ni] mpendwa wangu kwangu \q katika mashamba ya mizabibu ya En-gedi.
sw.B: Mpendwa wangu kwangu ni kishada cha maua ya hina \q katika mashamba ya mizabibu ya En-gedi.
sw.R: Mpendwa wangu ni kama kicha cha maua ya hina kwangu \q katika mashamba ya mizabibu ya En-gedi.

vi.L: Một chùm hoa lá móng [là] người yêu dấu của tôi đối với tôi \q trong các vườn nho Ên-ghê-đi.
vi.B: Người yêu dấu của tôi là chùm hoa lá móng đối với tôi \q trong các vườn nho Ên-ghê-đi.
vi.R: Người yêu của tôi như chùm hoa lá móng đối với tôi \q trong các vườn nho ở Ên-ghê-đi.

ko.L: 나의 사랑하는 이는 내게 헤나 꽃송이, \q 엔게디의 포도원들에 [있는 꽃송이이다].
ko.B: 내 사랑하는 이는 내게 헤나 꽃송이, \q 엔게디 포도원에 핀 꽃송이다.
ko.R: 내 사랑은 내게 헤나 꽃다발 같다. \q 엔게디 포도원에 핀 꽃 같다.

decisions.choice: henna: a shrub with sweet-smelling flowers
decisions.reason: Henna grows in warm places; its small white and yellow flowers hang in fragrant clusters, and its leaves give a red-orange dye (4:13).

decisions.choice: En-gedi: an oasis by the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: En-gedi is a spring on the western shore of the Dead Sea, green with gardens and vineyards in the middle of the desert (1 Samuel 24:1-2; Ezekiel 47:10).

decisions.choice: "alheña"
decisions.reason: "Alheña" is the Spanish name of the henna shrub (m1); "henna" is known mostly as the dye.

decisions.choice: "hoa lá móng"
decisions.reason: "Lá móng" is the Vietnamese name of the henna shrub, whose leaves are used to dye nails (m1); the plant keeps its name at every level, as the terms for the Song set.

decisions.choice: "헤나"
decisions.reason: "헤나" is the name Korean readers know for the plant and its dye (m1); "고벨화" is an older transcription that few readers would recognize.

source.text: הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ יָפָ֖ה עֵינַ֥יִךְ יוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, you [are] beautiful, my companion; look, you [are] beautiful; your eyes [are] doves.

en.L: Oh, you [are] beautiful, my companion! \q Oh, you [are] beautiful! Your eyes [are] doves.
en.B: How beautiful you are, my darling! \q How beautiful you are! Your eyes are doves.
en.R: My darling, you are so beautiful! \q So beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.

es.L: ¡Oh, [eres] hermosa, compañera mía! \q ¡Oh, [eres] hermosa! Tus ojos [son] palomas.
es.B: ¡Qué hermosa eres, amada mía! \q ¡Qué hermosa eres! Tus ojos son palomas.
es.R: Amada mía, ¡eres tan hermosa! \q ¡Tan hermosa! Tus ojos son como palomas.

fr.L: Oh, tu [es] belle, ma compagne ! \q Oh, tu [es] belle ! Tes yeux [sont] des colombes.
fr.B: Comme tu es belle, ma bien-aimée ! \q Comme tu es belle ! Tes yeux sont des colombes.
fr.R: Ma bien-aimée, tu es si belle ! \q Si belle ! Tes yeux sont comme des colombes.

sw.L: Lo, wewe [ni] mzuri, rafiki yangu! \q Lo, wewe [ni] mzuri! Macho yako [ni] njiwa.
sw.B: Jinsi ulivyo mzuri, mpenzi wangu! \q Jinsi ulivyo mzuri! Macho yako ni njiwa.
sw.R: Mpenzi wangu, wewe ni mzuri mno! \q Mzuri mno! Macho yako ni kama njiwa.

vi.L: Ôi, em [thật] xinh đẹp, bạn lòng của anh! \q Ôi, em [thật] xinh đẹp! Mắt em [là] bồ câu.
vi.B: Em đẹp biết bao, em yêu dấu! \q Em đẹp biết bao! Đôi mắt em là bồ câu.
vi.R: Em yêu, em đẹp quá! \q Đẹp quá! Đôi mắt em như chim bồ câu.

ko.L: 아, 그대는 아름답다, 나의 짝이여! \q 아, 그대는 아름답다! 그대의 눈은 비둘기[이다].
ko.B: 나의 연인이여, 그대는 얼마나 아름다운가! \q 얼마나 아름다운가! 그대의 눈은 비둘기다.
ko.R: 내 연인, 당신은 정말 아름다워요! \q 정말 아름다워요! 당신의 눈은 비둘기 같아요.

decisions.choice: the man speaks to the woman
decisions.reason: "You" and "beautiful" are feminine and he calls her "my companion" (1:9).

decisions.choice: your eyes are doves: soft, gentle and bright
decisions.reason: The picture may be the gentle look of a dove, the gray shimmer of its feathers, or eyes that flutter like doves. Doves stand for tenderness and faithfulness in the Song (2:14; 4:1; 5:2, 12; 6:9).

decisions.choice: Oh ... ; How beautiful
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens each line with a word that points ("look!"); English gives its force as an exclamation.

decisions.choice: "njiwa" for dove
decisions.reason: For the whole Song (2:14; 4:1; 5:2, 12; 6:9): "njiwa" is the everyday word for a dove or pigeon, and the terms for the Song use it in "njiwa wangu"; "hua" is the turtledove of 2:12.

source.text: הִנְּךָ֨יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ אַ֣ף נָעִ֔ים אַף־עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ רַעֲנָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, you [are] handsome, my beloved, yes, pleasant; yes, our couch [is] green.

en.L: Oh, you [are] handsome, my beloved, yes, delightful! \q Yes, our couch [is] green.
en.B: How handsome you are, my beloved, how delightful! \q Our couch is green and leafy.
en.R: My love, you are so handsome, so pleasant! \q The green grass will be our bed.

es.L: ¡Oh, [eres] hermoso, amado mío, sí, delicioso! \q Sí, nuestro lecho [es] verde.
es.B: ¡Qué hermoso eres, amado mío, qué encantador! \q Nuestro lecho es verde y frondoso.
es.R: Amor mío, ¡eres tan hermoso, tan agradable! \q La hierba verde será nuestra cama.

fr.L: Oh, tu [es] beau, mon bien-aimé, oui, délicieux ! \q Oui, notre lit [est] verdoyant.
fr.B: Comme tu es beau, mon bien-aimé, comme tu es charmant ! \q Notre lit est fait de verdure.
fr.R: Mon amour, tu es si beau, si agréable ! \q L’herbe verte sera notre lit.

sw.L: Lo, wewe [ni] mzuri, mpendwa wangu, naam, wa kupendeza! \q Naam, kitanda chetu [ni] kibichi.
sw.B: Jinsi ulivyo mzuri, mpendwa wangu, jinsi unavyopendeza! \q Kitanda chetu ni majani mabichi.
sw.R: Mpendwa wangu, wewe ni mzuri mno, unapendeza mno! \q Majani mabichi yatakuwa kitanda chetu.

vi.L: Ôi, anh [thật] khôi ngô, người yêu dấu của em, vâng, thật dễ mến! \q Vâng, giường của chúng ta [thì] xanh tươi.
vi.B: Anh khôi ngô biết bao, người yêu dấu của em, thật dễ mến! \q Giường của chúng ta là thảm lá xanh tươi.
vi.R: Anh yêu, anh thật đẹp trai, thật dễ thương! \q Cỏ xanh sẽ là giường của chúng ta.

ko.L: 아, 그대는 아름답다, 나의 사랑하는 이여, 참으로 사랑스럽다! \q 참으로 우리의 침상은 푸르다.
ko.B: 내 사랑하는 이여, 그대는 얼마나 멋지고 사랑스러운가! \q 우리의 침상은 푸르고 무성하다.
ko.R: 내 사랑, 당신은 정말 멋지고 다정해요! \q 푸른 풀밭이 우리의 침대가 될 거예요.

decisions.choice: the woman answers him
decisions.reason: "You" and "handsome" are masculine, and she calls him "my beloved": she answers his praise with her own.

decisions.choice: our couch is green: the lovers lie outdoors
decisions.reason: The word for green means fresh and leafy, as of a flourishing tree (Psalm 52:10; Jeremiah 11:16). Their bed is the grass under the trees, whose branches are the beams of their house (1:17).

decisions.choice: The green grass will be our bed
decisions.reason: Readable says what the green couch is (m2).

decisions.choice: "Kitanda chetu ni majani mabichi"
decisions.reason: "Kibichi" said of a bed would mean unripe or wet in Swahili; Balanced says what the green is, fresh leaves and grass (m2), and Literal keeps the bare word.

records.literal_gloss: [The] beams of our houses [are] cedars, our rafters cypresses.

en.L: The beams of our houses [are] cedars; \q our rafters [are] cypresses.
en.B: The beams of our house are cedars; \q our rafters are cypresses.
en.R: Cedar trees are the beams of our house. \q Cypress trees are its roof.

es.L: Las vigas de nuestras casas [son] cedros; \q nuestras viguetas [son] cipreses.
es.B: Las vigas de nuestra casa son cedros; \q nuestras viguetas, cipreses.
es.R: Los cedros son las vigas de nuestra casa. \q Los cipreses son su techo.

fr.L: Les poutres de nos maisons [sont] des cèdres ; \q nos chevrons [sont] des cyprès.
fr.B: Les poutres de notre maison sont des cèdres ; \q nos chevrons sont des cyprès.
fr.R: Les cèdres sont les poutres de notre maison. \q Les cyprès en sont le toit.

sw.L: Boriti za nyumba zetu [ni] mierezi; \q mapau yetu [ni] misunobari.
sw.B: Boriti za nyumba yetu ni mierezi; \q mapau yetu ni misunobari.
sw.R: Mierezi ndiyo boriti za nyumba yetu. \q Misunobari ndiyo paa lake.

vi.L: Các xà nhà của chúng ta [là] cây bá hương; \q rui mè của chúng ta [là] cây bách.
vi.B: Xà nhà của chúng ta là cây bá hương; \q rui nhà của chúng ta là cây bách.
vi.R: Cây bá hương là xà nhà của chúng ta. \q Cây bách là mái nhà.

ko.L: 우리 집들의 들보는 백향목[이고], \q 우리의 서까래는 잣나무[이다].
ko.B: 우리 집의 들보는 백향목이고, \q 우리의 서까래는 잣나무다.
ko.R: 백향목이 우리 집 들보이고, \q 잣나무가 우리 집 지붕이에요.

decisions.choice: cedars ... cypresses: the trees over them are their house
decisions.reason: The lovers picture the trees above them as the timber of a house. Cedar from Lebanon was the finest building wood (1 Kings 5:20-22). The second tree is named only here; it is probably a cypress or juniper.

decisions.choice: our houses: a plural that means one dwelling
decisions.reason: The plural may be a poetic way of speaking of one grand house. The verse continues the woman's words; it could also be the two lovers speaking together.

decisions.choice: Cedar trees ... Cypress trees ... its roof
decisions.reason: Readable says that the trees themselves are the house (m1) and calls the rafters a roof.

decisions.choice: "잣나무" for the second tree
decisions.reason: The published Kings (1 Kings 5:22; 6:34) render the cypress as "잣나무", and the Song keeps that word so the timber of Solomon's buildings and of the lovers' house is the same; the tree is not certain (m1).
